visualDecision.reason: The stated positions define an exact straight-track diagram and an ordered journey.

source.question: Explain distance, displacement, speed and velocity for JEE from the basics. Cover: frame of reference, origin and positive direction, why motion is relative; distance as path length versus displacement with a sign; average speed as total distance over time versus average velocity as displacement over time; instantaneous velocity dx/dt, speed as its magnitude. Draw one simple diagram: a straight track with A at x = 0, B at x = 40 m, C at x = 10 m, the car going A to B then back to C.

teachingTimeline.narration: Choose A as the origin and the direction toward B as positive. Position and motion depend on the observer's frame of reference; different observers can assign different velocities to the same car.

The car travels A to B, reverses, then stops at C. Distance adds both path lengths and never becomes negative. Displacement is final position minus initial position; the return leg is negative in this frame.
After adding the two path lengths, total distance is 70 m. The final position minus the initial position is +10 m, so the net displacement points in the positive direction.

For any positive total elapsed time Δt, average speed is 70 m divided by Δt, while average velocity is +10 m divided by Δt. No numerical rate is available without the time. Instantaneous velocity is the signed derivative dx/dt; instantaneous speed is its magnitude |v|. While moving on the return leg, the car's velocity is negative.
